newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET RATES STABLE IN QUIET TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET RATES STABLE IN QUIET TRADE.

text.p: Short term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted largely stable at their previous levels in quiet trade on Tuesday, dealers said.
"The market was fairly liquid under yesterday's (Monday's) date but there are no maturities today (Tuesday) and very little trade going on," a dealer said.
He said the market was still turning a blind eye on a four-week strike by Zimbabwean junior doctors and nurses demanding higher pay which has wreaked havoc on the country's health delivery system.
On Tuesday, discount houses were taking up treasury bills at 19.36 percent and selling the 91-day paper back to the market at a steady 19 percent.
NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were also being bought unchanged at 21 percent but bankers acceptance bills were quoted firmer at 20 percent from 19.50 percent on Monday.
Call money held steady at 18 percent in a market which was Z$770 million in surplus before settlement compared with Z$33 million the previous day.
